## **RRL Local Studies**

## **Acedo, G. G., et al. (2025).** Acedo et al. , developed a web-based document tracking system using QR-code technology for Catanduanes State University. “We gave each document a unique QR code so staff can see the status in real time instead of having to dig through paper files.” The overall rating of the system was excellent as per the ISO/IEC 25010 evaluation by the researchers. This study provides evidence for the use of QR tagging, a centralized database and ISO based pilot evaluation of SmartFlow. SmartFlow is different, as it is targeting municipal financial documents in the fields of Engineering, HR, Budget and Accounting in Urbiztondo. It leverages Flutter to scan at handoffs and React for registration, dashboards and COA-oriented reports. 

## **Piloton, A. J. L., et al. (2023).** Piloton et al. created a records tracking management system that utilizes QR code technology to replace the manual logbooks in a government records setting. The system kept track of file movement, user authentication, and kept an audit trail of who touched each record. The evaluators provided positive feedback on usability and accountability. SmartFlow applies this same principle at every inter-department handoff for disbursement vouchers, payroll records and approved budgets. Scan events are sent to a PHP REST API and stored in MySQL for reporting in the web portal. 

## **Aisporna, M. R., & Malicdem, E. K. (2024).** Aisporna and Malicdem developed a document routing and tracking system (DRTS) with a workflow management algorithm for the Local Government Unit of Magallanes, Philippines. The system enhanced the processing speed and accountability between departments and was rated as highly acceptable by the users. This is the strongest precedent for SmartFlow among local studies as it is not just a school or a single office but it addresses LGU inter-department routing. SmartFlow adds the ability to scan-in and scan-out on physical folders in Flutter, and flow summary reports aligned to the Chart of Accounts for the Municipal Accountant. 

## **Urmeneta, J. A., Agullo, J., et al. (2025).** Urmeneta et al. designed a digitized document tracking system that integrates QR code technology to record each movement in a verifiable audit trail. The study concluded that automated logging improves transparency and makes it easier to validate document history during review. SmartFlow applies the same accountability goal for Urbiztondo. The system does not digitize or store the content of voucher or payroll pages; it tracks only the movement of the paper packet, which matches the municipality’s current workflow.

## **Castro, R. B., et al. (2022).** Castro et al. built a web based system for tracking documents using barcode technology with SMS alerts on change of document status. The system knew which unit had the document and removed the uncertainty in routing from one location to another. SmartFlow leverages QR codes on a Flutter mobile app and web alerts on the React portal instead of SMS, negating additional telecom costs and targeting staff who already own smartphones. The study continues to confirm that automated notifications reduce the burden of manual follow-up. 

## **Balangat, E. S. (2022)**. Balangat assessed the records management system of LGU Calanasan and cited delayed submissions, poor accessibility of records and transparency in routing. The results are consistent with the interview with the Municipal Accountant of Urbiztondo who noted late documents from other departments and delays in consolidation through Excel. SmartFlow addresses that gap with real-time location on the dashboard, overdue flags, and department performance analytics to show which office is consistently slowing the flow. 

## **Tabia, V. U. (2022).**Tabia reviewed records management and data security in local government units and stressed the need for proper custody, accountability and protection of government information. This study supports the development of systems that log custody events without exposing extraneous personal data. SmartFlow captures office name, personnel, timestamp and document identifier on every scan. QR labels show only a tracking ID. Access to dashboards and exports on the web application is restricted by role. 

## **Web-based document tracking system**, DPWH Laguna II District Engineering Office (Philippine EJournals, 2022). Researchers developed a web-based system to register, track, and retrieve documents within a government engineering office. The study demonstrated that centralized tracking improves retrieval, reduces lost files, and strengthens control over document status. SmartFlow applies the same principle across four municipal offices and three financial document types that support COA preparation, rather than a single district engineering unit alone.

## **Docu-Go:** Web-based barangay document requesting system (IJITC, 2024). Docu-Go is a web-based system that allows residents to submit document requests and check status online, which reduces repeated visits and phone inquiries at the barangay hall. Although the context is barangay frontline service, the lesson applies inside Urbiztondo: staff currently use calls and group chats to ask whether a voucher or payroll packet was received. SmartFlow replaces informal status checks with logged scans and a shared React dashboard visible to authorized offices.

## **Gedorio, B. S., et al. (2023)**. Gedorio et al. evaluated a local government–related software system using the ISO/IEC 25010 software quality model and reported strong ratings in usability, reliability, and other characteristics. The results support using the same evaluation framework for LGU pilot systems. SmartFlow will use ISO/IEC 25010 during pilot testing with Accounting staff, department heads, and frontline clerks who perform daily scanning on Flutter.

## **RRL Foreign Studies**

## **Abdrabou-Adnan, L. (2023).** In Digitalization and Usage of QR-Code System in Documents Management, Abdrabou-Adnan linked each physical document file with a QR code, so that workers don’t anymore rummage through big paper piles trying to locate custody information. The research seems to back a hybrid pattern where paper still counts as the legal record, while digital logs keep the trail for location and historical notes. SmartFlow then mirrors that idea, for example disbursement vouchers, payroll records, and approved budgets, they move around municipal departments in Urbiztondo.

## **Peltokorpi, J., Isojärvi, L., Häkkinen, K., & Niemi, E. (2021).** In Peltokorpi et al. QR Code-Based Material Flow Monitoring in a Subcontractor Manufacturer Network, they found that QR scanning across different sites can funnel information into a central database, so material flow monitoring works across the whole network. Now in an LGU, each department office can be seen as a node, sort of like how routing networks behave. With SmartFlow, Engineering, HR, Budget and Accounting are treated as nodes, then Flutter is used for the scans at every handoff, while one PHP/MySQL server handles centralized monitoring, and React is used on the receiving side,

## **Hernandez, C., et al. (2023).** Hernandez et al. they implemented QR codes with a kind centralized monitoring dashboard, to help with tracking accuracy and easier data access for decision makers. In practice, field staff captured incidents via mobile scanning, while the administrators looked at overviews online , you know. SmartFlow kinda follows that same layout: decentralized scanning happens at each office, and then centralized monitoring is available for the Municipal Accountant, who also serves as the system administrator, through the web portal.

## **Li, X., et al. (2024).**Li et al. talked about security hazards in QR document setups, like meddling, spoofing, and yes technical defenses such as watermarking. Payroll and disbursement packets stay sensitive even when the only thing being watched is the movement, which sounds simple but it isnt. For SmartFlow, watermarking isn't there in version 1, though the papers pretty much back up things like secure login , role based access, and keeping the data on the printed QR codes to a minimum. If needed, more serious content protection stuff could be reviewed for later versions.

## **Lobonț, O., et al. (2025).**Lobonț et al. said office monitoring and compliance systems can fail if employees just skip steps in the procedure, kind of quietly. In their view, record tracing really depends on steady behavior at each receive , and also at every forward moment. That’s why SmartFlow basically asks for a scan at every handoff, and it comes with training for users who have low tech knowledge, as the Municipal Accountant mentioned during the needs assessment.

## **Marian, et al. (2025).** Marian et al. described audit flows that record which user accessed or moved a document, and at what time, creating a defensible chain of custody. SmartFlow produces a somewhat similar trail through scan-in and scan-out logs, with the document identifier, office, personnel, and a timestamp for Engineering HR Budget and Accounting, all in one place kinda.

## 

## **Alsuhibany , S. (2025)**. Alsuhibany cautioned that QR-based solutions alone cannot verify every legal or financial aspect of the content inside a high-stakes document. SmartFlow is scoped correctly as a movement and compliance support tool: it proves where and when a physical document traveled to support COA preparation, but not the numerical correctness of financial statements , which still stays the responsibility of the Accounting office.

SmartFlow’s COA-aligned summary module reports these indicators per department, helping the Municipal Accountant and management spot delays before audit deadlines show up.

Local studies by Acedo et al. (2025) and Gedorio et al. (2023) applied this model successfully. SmartFlow pilot testing will use the same eight criteria to see whether the hybrid system is fit for daily routine work in a small LGU, not just in theory.

## 

## **Synthesis of Related Literature and Studies**

## The policy literature from COA, DBM, PIDS, Republic Act No. 11032 , ADB, World Bank, and UN DESA suggests that local governments should improve the timeliness and traceability, plus keep the financial documents’ flow measurable—especially prior to COA consolidation. The Data Privacy Act of 2012 and records-management studies also nudge developers to log custody in a careful, sensible way. ISO/IEC 25010, then gives a standard approach to judge if a tracking system is acceptable to users.

## 

## In addition, the local studies show that QR codes, web portals, and LGU routing systems actually work in the Philippine context, without too much friction. Aisporna and Malicdem (2024) is the nearest LGU precedent, while Acedo et al. (2025) and Gedorio et al. (2023) back QR tracking together with ISO-based evaluation. Balangat (2022) feels like Urbiztondo’s situation, late submissions and weak transparency, kind of recurring in the same way.

## 

## The foreign studies confirm that physical documents can remain on paper while movement is tracked digitally (Abdrabou-Adnan, 2023; Peltokorpi et al., 2021), that central dashboards support management (Hernandez et al., 2023), and that user compliance at every handoff is critical (Lobonț et al., 2025).

SmartFlow uses QR codes on a Flutter mobile application and web-based alerts on React instead of SMS, for the four pilot offices in Urbiztondo.

**Balangat, E. S. (2022)**. Balangat studied the records management system of LGU Calanasan and reported delayed submissions, poor accessibility, and lack of transparency. These problems are similar to the interview findings in Urbiztondo, where the Municipal Accountant cited late documents from other departments and manual counting in Excel. SmartFlow addresses this with real-time location, overdue flags, and department performance analytics to identify slow offices.

**Tabia, V. U. (2022).** Tabia examined records management and data security in local government units and emphasized proper custody and accountability. SmartFlow supports this by logging office, user, and time on every scan and by printing only a tracking identifier on QR labels, not sensitive personal data.

Web-based document tracking system, DPWH Laguna II District Engineering Office **(Philippine EJournals, 2022).** Researchers developed a web system to register, track, and retrieve documents within a government engineering office. The study showed that centralized tracking improves retrieval and control. SmartFlow applies the same goal across four municipal offices and three financial document types that support COA preparation.

Docu-Go: Web-based barangay document requesting system **(IJITC, 2024\)**. Docu-Go allows residents to submit requests and check status online, which reduces repeated visits to the barangay hall. The lesson for SmartFlow is the same: Urbiztondo staff currently use phone calls and group chats to ask whether a document was received. SmartFlow replaces informal follow-ups with logged scans and a shared React dashboard.

**Gedorio, B. S., et al. (2023)**. Gedorio et al. evaluated a local government–related software system using the ISO/IEC 25010 quality model and reported strong ratings across usability and reliability. SmartFlow will use ISO/IEC 25010 during pilot testing with Accounting staff, department heads, and frontline clerks who use the Flutter application.

## **Foreign Studies (RRS)**

**Abdrabou-Adnan, L. (2023)**. Abdrabou-Adnan studied QR-code digitalization for document management while keeping physical files. Each file folder was linked to a QR code so staff no longer searched through paper stacks. SmartFlow uses the same paper-plus-digital-trail approach for disbursement vouchers, payroll records, and approved budgets in Urbiztondo.

**Peltokorpi, J., Isojärvi, L., Häkkinen, K., & Niemi, E. (2021)**. Peltokorpi et al. tested QR code-based material flow monitoring across multiple locations in a supply network. Scans at each location fed a central database for monitoring. In SmartFlow, each department acts like a location: clerks scan on Flutter, and data is centralized in PHP and MySQL for the React dashboard.

**Hernandez, C., et al. (2023)**. Hernandez et al. implemented QR codes with a centralized monitoring dashboard to improve tracking and data access. SmartFlow follows the same pattern: decentralized scanning at each office and centralized monitoring for the Municipal Accountant, who also serves as the system administrator, on the web portal.

**Li, X., et al. (2024)**. Li et al. discussed security risks in QR-based document systems, including tampering and spoofing. SmartFlow addresses these risks through HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens that are verified server-side on every scan; tampered or forged labels are rejected before any record is written, and tokens expire after a fixed validity period. The system also enforces role-based access and encodes minimal data on printed QR labels.

**Lobonț, O., et al. (2025)**. Lobonț et al. reported that office monitoring systems fail when employees do not follow required steps. SmartFlow depends on scanning at every receive and forward; training and a simple Flutter interface address low technology knowledge noted by the Municipal Accountant.

**Marian, et al. (2025)**. Marian et al. described audit flows that record which user accessed or moved a document and when. SmartFlow scan-in and scan-out logs provide the same chain of custody for Engineering, HR, Budget, and Accounting.

**Alsuhibany, S. (2025)**. Alsuhibany cautioned that QR-based systems alone cannot verify all legal or financial content inside a document. SmartFlow is scoped correctly: it proves where and when a document moved to support COA preparation, not the figures inside financial statements (those remain with Accounting).

**United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (2024)**. UN DESA e-government materials recommend measuring turnaround time, overdue workload, and completion rates. SmartFlow’s COA-oriented flow summaries report average processing time per department, late submission counts, and completion rates.

**International Organization for Standardization (2011)** — ISO/IEC 25010\. ISO/IEC 25010 defines eight software quality characteristics used to evaluate systems in a structured way. SmartFlow pilot testing will use this model, consistent with local studies by Acedo et al. (2025) and Gedorio et al. (2023).

**Rimando, M. K. V., & Corpuz, R. R. (2022)**. Rimando and Corpuz built a real-time QR tracking system with added security features for documents in transit. SmartFlow does not require watermarking in the first version, but the study supports protecting audit log integrity for sensitive financial documents in an LGU.

## **Synthesis of Related Studies**

In general , the local studies show that QR codes , web portals, and LGU routing systems do work in the Philippine context, kind of like expected. There’s also Aisporna and Malicdem (2024) that seems to be the strongest LGU precedent, while Acedo et al. (2025) and Gedorio et al. (2023) back up QR tracking as well as the ISO/IEC 25010 evaluation. On the other hand, the international studies say that physical documents may stay on paper , but the movement is still traced digitally (Abdrabou-Adnan, 2023 Peltokorpi et al., 2021).
